relationships.description: The parent container physically owns a child container that exists only within it, such as a partition, hypertable chunk, or Firestore subcollection, and that child is dropped when the parent is dropped.
relationships.evidence: DDL such as CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF parent, TimescaleDB chunk metadata, or a subcollection path nested under the parent document collection.

relationships.description: The collection owns the trigger, change-stream subscription, or watcher registered against it, and that handler is removed when the collection is dropped.
relationships.evidence: A CREATE TRIGGER ... ON <table> statement, a change-stream watch() call scoped to the collection, or a CDC connector config naming the table.

relationships.description: The collection's physical structure is made up of the column, document path, or property, which holds a stored value for each record and has no existence outside that collection.
relationships.evidence: The column appears in the table's CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN DDL, a document JSON schema, or a search-index mapping.

relationships.description: The engine maintains the index as a lookup structure over this collection's records, and the index is dropped along with the collection.
relationships.evidence: A CREATE INDEX ... ON <table> statement, a createIndex call on the collection, or an index definition in the collection's mapping or migration file.

relationships.description: As modeled, the collection contains the schema, keyspace, or named graph, which would make the namespace a part that cannot exist without the collection.
relationships.evidence: A catalog entry or DDL showing the namespace created inside and dependent on the table, which real engines do not normally support.

relationships.description: The collection carries the engine-enforced constraint, such as a CHECK, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, or $jsonSchema validator, which restricts writes to it and exists only as part of its definition.
relationships.evidence: A CONSTRAINT clause in the table DDL, an ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT migration, or a collMod/createCollection validator option on the collection.

relationships.description: The physical table or collection is the concrete data object that the access-control model's protected resource stands for, so authorization decisions about the resource apply to its records.
relationships.evidence: GRANT statements, row-level security policies, or IAM resource ARNs that name the table, linked to the resource entry in the authorization model.

relationships.description: Fields of the payload a client submits to an operation are persisted into this collection's columns or document fields.
relationships.evidence: An ORM entity or DTO-to-entity mapper that converts the request payload class into a row of the table, or a handler that inserts the parsed body into the collection.

relationships.description: The collection is the persistent store in which instances of the business concept, such as Orders or Claims, are recorded across their lifecycle.
relationships.evidence: A data dictionary or ORM entity annotated with the table name that documents it as the system of record for the business entity.

relationships.description: The collection's record structure is the stored form of the API data shape, so the schema's properties correspond to the collection's persisted fields.
relationships.evidence: OpenAPI components/schemas generated from, or annotated with, the ORM entity that maps to the table, or a model class shared by the schema and the table mapping.

relationships.description: Records in one collection hold keys or identifiers that point to records in another collection, without the referencing collection depending on it to function.
relationships.evidence: A FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES clause, an ObjectId/DBRef field naming the other collection, or a graph edge type whose endpoints are the other node label.

relationships.description: The collection meets the handling obligations of the sensitivity tier assigned to its data, such as encryption at rest or restricted access.
relationships.evidence: Storage configuration enabling encryption or masking on the table, together with a data catalog tag assigning the classification label to it.

relationships.description: The collection's structure, retention, or storage characteristics fulfill a stated need, such as keeping an audit history or storing a required data attribute.
relationships.evidence: A requirement ID referenced in the migration, schema comment, or design doc that introduces the table, plus a test or acceptance check verifying it.

relationships.description: The collection provides persistent storage and retrieval of records that the application component reads and writes to carry out its responsibilities.
relationships.evidence: A repository, DAO, or ORM model inside the component's codebase that queries or writes the table, or the component's datasource configuration listing it.

relationships.description: The collection supplies the stored data that the application service's operations read and modify to deliver their offered behavior.
relationships.evidence: The service implementation's methods invoke repository queries against the table, as shown in code or in service-to-data traceability documentation.

relationships.description: The collection is the data source from which the API operation's handler retrieves or persists records to fulfill requests on that method and path.
relationships.evidence: The route handler or controller action bound to the method-path pair issues queries or writes against the table, directly or through a repository.

notes: composes namespace is inverted: namespaces contain collections. Collection-composes-collection is valid only for partitions or subcollections. maps-to requestbody overlaps realizes schema, since request bodies are expressed through schemas. implements secureresource could equally be realizes. serves applicationcomponent and serves applicationservice partly duplicate each other.
